seal.statement: During preparation and execution the comparative campaign never obtains an image, a harness commit or a reference-client package from the network on its own initiative and never substitutes another source or outcome when one is missing: an absent image is a typed image_unavailable refusal naming host, role and image, with --pull=never on every campaign docker run; an absent harness commit is a typed load_generator_commit_absent refusal before any worktree exists; the reference client installs offline only and a missing tarball is a typed offline_cache_incomplete refusal naming it; a host whose thermal decision cannot be read stays excluded and the exclusion carries a typed reason. Placement of images, the harness commit and the reference-client cache is an explicit provisioning step that exists in code for every supported target (the home lab and GCP), so no target that worked before is left with only a refusal.

SUPERSESSION RECORD (R09), 2026-11-14, by the lead. The sealed statement says provisioning 'exists in code for every supported target (the home lab and GCP)'. For the home lab that clause was wrong as written: by the owner's standing rule lab machines are reached only through the local lab controller, which is deliberately not part of this repository, so repository code must not place anything on lab hosts by itself. Replacement: for GCP, placement is repository code (the provisioning script and the --provision command, verified against the campaign's own checks); for the home lab, placement is an explicit operator step performed through the lab controller route (image save/load between hosts at the capped rate, the campaign checkout from a git bundle, the reference-client package cache), documented in the reproduction guide and the measurement runbook, and the campaign's typed refusals name exactly what a host lacks. The constraint no-working-path-broken is met for the lab by that documented operator step having been carried out and proven: postgres:17-alpine placed on adam-laptop by save/load with a matching image id, storage roots and campaign checkouts created on the hosts, the reference client installed offline, and the real-lab dry run c6fa8a7f passing with the intended roles. Nothing here weakens the refusals. Evidence ceiling stated by the writer and kept: GCP provisioning is proven against scripted hosts only; nothing was executed on GCP.
